Hello everyone, they say that correcting course is a sign of wisdom, so I have rethought my repository and reduced it to presenting "only" the protocol I require for my work. I leave you the link in case you are interested. https://github.com/Alektronnik/M4TH/blob/main/M4THDocs/M4THProtocol.md. Having a rigorous protocol and much, much dedication can help create serious, compilable, and professional projects. But this is only the final phase; working with multiple LLMs involves much more than this. The first thing is not to limit yourself to a single model, but to have multiple LLMs, depending on the phase of the project you are in and the needs to be covered. Each model has special characteristics and even a bias. They also have different capacities for context, vision, or specialize in programming code, so using a single LLM model for a project is totally discouraged. At a minimum, incorporate a system of 3 independent models to be able to have PLANNING, DEVELOPMENT, and REVIEW. Likewise, assign these functions according to the skills of the models you have available. In the process, it is important to clearly define the objectives and rules they must follow. And most importantly, it is a job that must be directed, reviewed, and validated by the user, who is the responsible party and author of everything that is generated and created. Something else that will help you is having a template for each type of file you are going to work on and the main thing: "standardize repetitive processes, read and review every generated code or text, and put in hours and hours." Lastly, get used to bearing the stigma "Created by AI and not by human" for a while; but soon, the label will be different, perhaps Metahuman would be the most appropriate definition. Time will tell. Any questions you may have about this or the 15 packages that have been formalized and are public, I am at your disposal.

Alektronnik (P.S. Following rules when I've never followed them)
